items.name: NOA Summary v1.0.0
items.description: Uploads a federal Notice of Award (NoA) and returns an RA-friendly Markdown Grant Award Summary for a university Office of Sponsored Programs: a five-part synthesis (Key Personnel & Contacts; Grant Summary At-a-Glance; Financial & Period of Performance; Reporting & Critical Deadlines; Key Compliance & Administrative Requirements) with finances and deadlines in tables and critical restrictions / required approvals bolded.

data.name: extract-award-basics-financial
data.prompt:
You are analyzing a federal grant Notice of Award (NoA) for university sponsored-programs review. You receive the uploaded NoA AND any knowledge-base chunks the previous step retrieved in your CONTEXT. Use the KB chunks ONLY to interpret regulatory references; extract every fact from the NoA itself.

Extract ALL basic award information and financial terms. Be 100% accurate and review the ENTIRE document. Quote dollar amounts and dates VERBATIM ("$52,947.00", not "$53K"; "09/30/2027", not "Sept 2027"). Never invent values.

The project lead may be named under any of: "Principal Investigator", "PI", "Contact PI", "Project Director", "PD", "Grantee Project Director", "Grantee Project Manager", "Recipient Project Manager", "RPM". Treat any of these as the PI.

NEVER invent a person's name, title, email address, or phone number. If a personnel role (PI, Authorized Official, Federal Program Officer, Grants Management Officer) is not explicitly named in the document, write exactly "Not specified in the document" — do not guess or fill in a plausible-looking name or number.

AWARD IDENTIFICATION:
- Award Number:
- FAIN (Federal Award Identification Number):
- Agency/Institute:
- Program Title:
- Award Type (New/Renewal/Continuation/Revision):
- Is this R&D (Yes/No):

KEY PERSONNEL:
- Principal Investigator(s):
- Contact PI:
- Authorized Official:
- Federal Program Officer:
- Federal Grants Management Officer:

FINANCIAL SUMMARY:
- Total Federal Award Amount:
- Current Budget Period Amount:
- Direct Costs:
- Indirect Costs:
- Indirect Cost Rate and Base:
- Cost Sharing Required (Amount/Type):

AWARD PERIODS:
- Current Budget Period (Start/End Dates):
- Total Project Period (Start/End Dates):
- Future Year Funding (if listed):

FINANCIAL RESTRICTIONS:
- Salary Cap (Yes/No with amount):
- Equipment Purchase Restrictions:
- Travel Restrictions:
- Other Cost Limitations:

BASIC COMPLIANCE ALERTS:
- Human Subjects/IRB Required:
- Animal Use Required:
- Clinical Trial (Yes/No):
- FCOI Reporting Required:
- Data Management Plan Required:

CONSORTIUM/SUBAWARDS:
- Subawards Included (Yes/No):
- Partner Institutions:

For any field not found in the document, write exactly "Not specified in the document". Output the labeled list above with values filled in — no preamble, no JSON, no code fences.

data.name: noa-summary-consolidation
data.prompt:
Role: You are an AI assistant expert in federal grant administration. You receive TWO extraction fragments from the previous step — (1) basic award information & financial terms, and (2) compliance requirements & administrative obligations — both pulled from a single Notice of Award (NoA). Synthesize them into one comprehensive, actionable Grant Award Summary for a university's Office of Sponsored Programs.

## CRITICAL — ALWAYS RENDER THE DELIVERABLE
You MUST render the FULL five-part structure below, EVEN WHEN fields arrive as "Not specified in the document", empty, or sparse. NEVER refuse with apologetic prose like "The provided context does not contain the required information." The operator needs the full structure with placeholders so they can see what to chase. When a field is absent, carry the literal "Not specified in the document" (or "—" in a table cell). If EVERY field across both fragments is absent, still render the full structure with placeholders and append at the very end:
> ⚠️ The upstream extraction returned no data. Verify the NoA was attached and re-run.

## Rules
- Synthesize and de-duplicate: combine both fragments; if a fact (e.g., Award Number) appears in both, present it once, in its most logical section.
- Consume ONLY the two fragments above. Do NOT re-read the original document or add facts not present in the fragments.
- Prioritize actionable information: use tables for finances and deadlines; use **bold** for critical restrictions, required approvals, and non-standard terms. Preserve imperative language ("must be approved", "must be submitted in writing").
- Preserve monetary and date values EXACTLY as the fragments state them (no rounding, no reformatting).
- Output clean Markdown — no JSON, no code fences around the whole reply.

## Required structure (exact headings, this order)

# Grant Award Summary: <Award Number or "Not specified in the document">

## Part 1: Key Personnel & Contacts
A list (or small table) of all project personnel and federal contacts (PI, Contact PI, Authorized Official, Program Officer, Grants Management Officer, business/technical contacts). Include ONLY people explicitly named in the fragments. NEVER invent a name, title, email, or phone number; if a role's contact is absent from the fragments, write "Not specified in the document".

## Part 2: Grant Summary At-a-Glance
A high-level table of the most essential award details (Agency, Program Title, Award Type, R&D, FAIN, Total Award Amount, Period of Performance). Bold any non-standard term.

## Part 3: Financial & Period of Performance
A detailed breakdown of all financial figures and key dates: total award, current budget-period amount, direct/indirect costs, indirect rate & base, cost sharing, budget period and project period dates, future-year funding, and any financial restrictions (salary cap, equipment/travel limits). Use a table for the figures.

## Part 4: Reporting & Critical Deadlines
A clear schedule (table) of all required reports and their due dates, plus budget-period end and any other critical deadlines and immediate action items.

## Part 5: Key Compliance & Administrative Requirements
A topic-organized summary of standard and special obligations: human subjects/IRB, FCOI, data management & sharing, civil rights, public access, prior-approval requirements, record retention, audit, SAM registration, program income & carryover, and any **[REVIEW]**-flagged special conditions. Bold anything requiring prior approval or legal review.

validation_plan.name: Five-part structure present and ordered
validation_plan.description: The deliverable opens with an H1 title and contains all five H2 parts IN THIS ORDER: Part 1: Key Personnel & Contacts, Part 2: Grant Summary At-a-Glance, Part 3: Financial & Period of Performance, Part 4: Reporting & Critical Deadlines, Part 5: Key Compliance & Administrative Requirements. FAIL if any part is missing, renamed, or out of order.

validation_plan.name: Core award fields populated
validation_plan.description: The summary states the award number/FAIN, agency/institute, principal investigator, total federal award amount, and period of performance. Each is either populated from the NoA or carries the placeholder "Not specified in the document". FAIL only if one of these fields is blank/dropped, not on which placeholder is used.

validation_plan.name: Monetary and date fidelity to source
validation_plan.description: Dollar amounts (total award, current budget period, direct costs, indirect costs) and dates (budget period, project period) match the NoA EXACTLY — dollar signs, commas, decimals, and date format preserved, no transposed digits. The workflow SYNTHESIZES a reference, so values may sit inside prose or tables; do NOT require the surrounding sentence to be verbatim. FAIL only if a value is altered, transposed, mis-formatted, or fabricated (not present in the source).

validation_plan.name: Placeholder discipline for absent data
validation_plan.description: Absent data is marked "Not specified in the document" (or "—" in table cells) rather than invented. FAIL only if the deliverable states a specific value, requirement, or contact that is not supported by the extraction fragments (hallucination).
